summary: Risk-on came back with force and the turn is confirmed. The Nasdaq ran 3.4 percent to 28,004 and held well above its stop, the S&P reclaimed its own stop (up 2.3 percent) to confirm, gold rallied with stocks (up 1.9 percent) and VIX collapsed 22 percent to 19.98. Crude was the lone decliner, down 3.9 percent through 90 and its stop. A big day runs straight into tomorrow's October CPI, so chasing here pays little.

risk.note: Throttle eased from REDUCED as volatility normalized (VIX 19.98, back under 20) and the equity trend stopped being split. The caveat is the calendar: the October CPI prints Tuesday Nov 10 at 8:30 AM ET, a binary event, so keep event risk small into the print. Veterans Day Wednesday Nov 11 (bond market closed, equity futures open); next policy event the December FOMC.

psychology: The hardest trade today was trusting a move you already missed. After Thursday's washout and Friday's fade, a clean gap-up that holds tempts you to fade it out of disbelief. Let the level prove itself, then follow, instead of betting against strength because it feels too fast. With CPI tomorrow, sizing up late in a stretched move is how one number undoes a good week.

yesterdaysMapScore.note: Published Nov 6 for the Monday Nov 9 session. The map hedged a reclaim against a renewed loss. Monday delivered a confirmed risk-on trend: MNQ played out its reclaim-and-extend branch, MES played out its reclaim-confirms branch, gold played out its hold-and-stabilize branch, and crude's up bias failed while the row's own downside branch played out. The one not-triggered row was the MNQ downside loss, which never set up.
